name: Hyperboreans

attributes.attribute: a people called beyond the north wind, peaceful vegetarians with magical powers
worshiped Apollo in a circular stone temple linked with Stonehenge
Greek writers identified them as the Celts by the fourth century B.C.E.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Hyperboreans were a Celtic people. The ancient Greeks recorded their existence. The name means beyond the north wind. The Greeks saw them as a semi-mythological people with magical powers. These peaceful vegetarians worshiped Apollo. Their great stone temple was circular, and some linked it with Stonehenge. Most ancient geographers placed the Hyperborean homeland in Europe, not on Britain. By the fourth century B.C.E. Greek authors said the people of the alleged homeland were the ones they called Celts. This adopted one of the names the Celts used for themselves, which meant the lofty ones or the warriors.

okr.objective: Document the Hyperboreans, the northern people the Greeks identified as Celts.
key_results: Record the name meaning beyond the north wind and the semi-mythical status.
Describe their worship of Apollo and the circular stone temple linked with Stonehenge.
Note how Greek writers came to call them Celts.
